rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a transfer-learning surrogate model for HfNbTiVAl10, while the paper used a rule-of-mixtures modulus screening and VEC-based selection to design a specific Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W composition. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (computational modeling vs. alloy design and experimental validation).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions room-temperature tensile and fracture testing, whereas the paper performed room-temperature quasi-static compression on as-cast specimens. The loading mode (tension/fracture vs. compression) and the material system differ, so only the broad room-temperature regime is shared.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis relies on a deep-learning surrogate with physics constraints to predict properties, while the paper's mechanism is reducing VEC to promote dislocation mobility and delay brittle cracking. These are different classes of mechanism (computational prediction vs. physical deformation mechanism).
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts Young's modulus, yield strength, and toughness for HfNbTiVAl10, whereas the paper reports compressive yield strength, fracture strain, and hardness for a Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W alloy. The properties and material system differ, so there is no agreement on the specific outcome.
